title: Scout Finding (one entry of a ronin scout's returned array)
description:
Versioned contract for a single ronin scout finding — the re-measurement a ronin-{bow,sword,brush,arts} agent returns for one reflex (or one constituent of a correlation reflex), consumed by sensei-cycle Step 4 to decide which findings reach the rival verifier. Draft-07 is mandatory, not stylistic: ajv 6.15.0 (api/package.json) rejects 2020-12 outright while Python jsonschema 4.26 accepts it, so a 2020-12 schema passes the Python tests and silently fails on the TS side.

DERIVED FROM THE DOCUMENTED CONTRACT, NOT FROM HISTORY. There is no scout-finding corpus: state/ronin_results/*.json holds four singletons with divergent shapes ({status,item_id,reason,detail} / {status,item_id,metric,commit_hash,detail} / {status}) which are remediation-item results, not scout findings. The authority is the Output block of sub-bundles/claude/agents/ronin-*.md plus sensei-cycle SKILL.md Steps 3-4. Validate this against NEW scout runs, not against ronin_results.

reflex_id.description: Echoed verbatim from the batch input, so a flattened multi-pillar finding array stays attributable.

real.description: Did the LIVE re-measurement reproduce the breach? false + fixability 'phantom' means the wid_payload snapshot was stale.

evidence.description: The re-measurement itself. Open object — metrics differ in what they can cite — but re_measured and source_file are the two the rival independently re-derives against, so both are required. Absence of data is never healthy: an unresolvable source is a finding (real:false, fixability:structural), not an empty evidence block.

source_file.description: One path, or the list of paths when a metric is derived from several. minLength/minItems each constrain only their own type — an empty citation is not a citation.

proposed_fix.description: A command, or null when the finding is a phantom and there is nothing to fix.

target_repo.description: Where the fix would land — determined per finding, never assumed from the scout's pillar. Null on the same condition proposed_fix is null: a phantom finding has nothing to fix, so it has nowhere to land. Added 2026-07-28 after the first ARMED cycle — ronin-bow correctly returned a phantom with target_repo:null and the schema logged a violation for it, which would have held A3's 'seven clean days' gate permanently unreachable, since phantoms are a normal scout outcome. null is listed in the enum as well as the type: draft-07 checks enum by exact value, so a nullable type alone would still fail here.

risk_tier.description: 'security' whenever the proposed fix touches security controls (hooks, gates, scrubbers) — those are ALWAYS manual, so the value gates automation.

fixability.description: 'structural' routes to backlog escalation (SKILL.md Step 7); 'phantom' means suppress, not remediate.

else.description: Nullability of target_repo/proposed_fix is tied to phantom, not granted outright. Making target_repo nullable for phantoms (2026-07-28) otherwise also let a REAL finding — fixability 'code' or 'skill', something a remediation is expected to act on — validate with nowhere to land and nothing to run. Warn-only today and nothing reads target_repo yet, so this is inert; it stops being inert the moment A3 flips enforcement or remediation starts routing on the field, and the schema should not be the thing that has to be remembered then.
